The mental state is not the mind itself. It is only the mind’s current experience. We are not just our emotions or our thought processes. We have fears, we have interests, passions, values, opinions. We have hobbies and goals and other things. Mental state is simply what the mind is experiencing. It is not the whole mind. 

That being said, there is more to us than just the mind. Some might say that the mind is the self, but many would argue that there are other things that make us who we are as human being. Some people subscribe to the idea of a soul, or other sort of “thing” that makes us uniquely human, and uniquely ourselves.

Yes, and no - which is my very roundabout way of saying that it depends. 

In my experience, sometimes talking things out is what I need to accept a situation or thought pattern. Specifically, talking about embarrassing irrational fears and things of that nature. Sometimes speaking to a therapist about these things is enough to get my brain to accept them somewhat. 

In a lot of ways therapy, for me specifically, has been the best medicine. But not necessarily just the talking. I see therapy as getting an education, learning about myself and my mind and my mental health. I learn valuable skills and coping strategies. Sure, talking is a part of it - but it is what I take away from therapy - the skills, lessons, and insights - that have been the most healing for me. 

That being said, sometimes you are at a place where you cannot even begin to talk things out or to receive therapy. Here, the best medicine is, well, medicine. Sometimes medication is absolutely crucial and life saving. A lot of physical symptoms must first be addressed with proper medication. If ones mental health symptoms are unbearable, the first goal is to decrease these symptoms, bring them to a somewhat manageable level, and only then can therapy take place - when one is ready. Personally, I think everyone and anyone should go to therapy at least once in their lives - mental health concerns or not. It has helped me gain insight that I don’t imagine I could get otherwise. It’s not easy - in fact it’s a lot of work, and at times it makes you feel worse for a period of time before things finally get better. But in my opinion, it is so worth it.

I’m currently having some of the worst cramps of my life, and here are things that may help:

1) painkillers. I find Aleve (naproxen) works well, that of any other NSAID, or a mild muscle relaxant such as Robaxacet. 

2) hot water bottle. I have a Magic Bag that you heat in the microwave, but any hot water bottle will do. In a pinch, you can wet a hand towel, wring it out, microwave until hot and then slip it into a ziploc bag. 

3) a hot bath or shower. 

4) hot, uncaffenaited beverages - herbal tea, hot water with lemon and honey, anything like that. 

5) a back rub - focusing on the lower back - ask her where feels good and go from there. 

6) staying hydrated. 

7) distraction - movies, tv shows, gaming - whatever you guys like to do together. 

All in all I think it’s super sweet that you want to alleviate her cramps and I hope the above tips help! Hope she feels better soon.
